_note: ROUND 6 R6-09. The baseline the npm ratchet compares against: ADVISORY IDS, not counts.
THE DEFECT THIS REPLACES. scripts/verify-npm-audit-policy.sh compared the NUMBER of vulnerable
packages per severity plus an allowlist of package NAMES. A brand new high-severity advisory on
`next`, `ws`, `sharp` or `postcss`, all already vulnerable and already allowlisted, changes
neither the count nor the name, so the gate stayed green. Its own header claimed it 'fails on
anything worse: a new high, a new critical', and that was simply false.
An advisory ID is an identity. A new ID means something genuinely new arrived, whatever package
it attaches to and whatever the totals do. Adding an ID here is ACCEPTING a vulnerability and
belongs in a commit that says why, with the reachability argument in the script's header.
Measured 2026-08-08 with npm audit --omit=dev. Re-measure with scripts/verify-npm-audit-policy.sh
by re-reading the FAIL output of scripts/verify-npm-audit-policy.sh, which prints every id
it refused. An earlier note pointed at a --print-baseline flag that was never implemented.
_accepted_2026_08_14: 1139427 nanoid high, GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8, 'custom generators can loop indefinitely when
size is zero', range <3.3.18. Transitive under `next`, which uses nanoid for build ids.
The loop needs a CUSTOM generator called with size 0; nothing in this repo calls nanoid at
all, so there is no call site to reach it from. Build-time, and a denial of service rather
1139510 postcss high, GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849, path traversal in previous-source-map
auto-loading via sourceMappingURL, disclosing an arbitrary .map file. Range <=8.5.17,
transitive under `next`. postcss processes OUR OWN CSS at build time and does not ship to
the browser, so the sourceMappingURL it would follow comes from globals.css and Tailwind
output, both written by us. Reaching it requires control of a CSS file we compile.
NO FIX AVAILABLE THAT IS PROPORTIONATE TODAY. `npm audit fix --omit=dev` offers nothing for
either. Both live under `next` 15.5.22, and the only route is a version bump; latest is
16.3.1, a MAJOR. Doing that hours after deploying the mainnet cutover, on launch day, to
close two build-time issues with no reachable path, is the wrong trade. Tracked as a follow-up
in private/ROADMAP_POST_LAUNCH.md rather than left implicit here.
